model_summary: GitHub raw authority CAS/precondition is represented as (authority_source_revision, authority_observed_raw_digest) pair, distinct from Subject CAS and normalized semantic digest. Subject revision never used as GitHub CAS; normalized digest never used as raw CAS.

domains.purpose: Subject aggregate CAS (M4-5/M3-B6 durable subject graph)

domains.type: authority_source_revision: str|int opaque GitHub revision token; authority_observed_raw_digest: SHA-256 hex of raw body bytes
domains.purpose: GitHub optimistic write precondition (external authority CAS)
semantic validation and drift comparison only; supporting evidence, never external CAS

GITHUB_RAW_AUTHORITY_REVISION_SOURCE.description: Opaque GitHub raw authority revision/source token observed at read time, not derived or fabricated by adapter. Must be treated as opaque by Core; adapter plumbing may obtain it from the authoritative GitHub Issue read path.
GITHUB_RAW_AUTHORITY_REVISION_SOURCE.chosen_model: Opaque external revision token + observed_raw_digest pair — adapter captures whatever authoritative revision the GitHub read provides as an opaque string/int (e.g., updated_at ISO-8601 as string, or ETag-like opaque token, or monotonic revision if the store exposes one). Adapter MUST NOT assume ETag validity without source evidence; MUST NOT substitute comment ID for revision; MUST NOT synthesize updated_at if not provided. The pair (revision_token, observed_raw_digest) together form the CAS precondition; comparison requires both (revision equality and digest equality) to disambiguate concurrent races.
GITHUB_RAW_AUTHORITY_REVISION_SOURCE.why_not_single_assumption_without_eviden: Plan forbids assuming one of updated_at/ETag/node ID/comment ID/body hash without authority/source evidence. GitHub Issue API does not document a native conditional write ETag for Issue body updates in the REST shape the adapter uses; the adapter therefore must NOT claim native CAS; it must perform read-before-write with explicit raw precondition compare and verify-after-write, documenting revision source as observed opaque token.

GITHUB_RAW_AUTHORITY_DIGEST_SOURCE.description: SHA-256 hex of exact raw authoritative body bytes as observed at read time (authority_observed_raw_digest) and of exact intended candidate raw bytes (candidate_raw_digest). For Issue body, digest is over raw body string bytes; for comments, over comment body bytes.
GITHUB_RAW_AUTHORITY_DIGEST_SOURCE.computation: canonical source bytes as returned by GitHub read (preserving exact bytes modulo bounded normalization), hashed via SHA-256 hex; candidate digest computed from exact candidate_raw_body string supplied in PortablePlanMutationRequest; comparison is exact raw identity (byte-level exact, not semantic normalized equality)
GITHUB_RAW_AUTHORITY_DIGEST_SOURCE.candidate_vs_normalized_distinct: candidate_raw_digest (exact external document identity) vs normalized_plan_digest (semantic normalized digest) are separate domains; normalized equality alone never proves exact external effect (J8/CONFLICT)

steps: read exact current raw authority via readRawAuthority (returns current_raw_revision, current_raw_digest, raw_body)
retrieve authorized precondition stored in PortablePlanMutationRequest / JournalRecord PREPARED (authority_source_revision, authority_observed_raw_digest, candidate_raw_digest)
compare current_raw_revision == expected authority_source_revision (if expected is not None)
compare current_raw_digest == expected authority_observed_raw_digest (if expected is not None)
if either mismatch (revision mismatch OR digest mismatch) -> stale raw authority -> fail closed with STALE_AUTHORITY; no external write
only if both match (or expected None intentionally omitted with explicit bounded rule) -> eligible to proceed to external attempt after journal PREPARED->APPLYING durability

native_cas_note: Even with correct (revision+digest) CAS mapping, the underlying GitHub API operation today provides no usable native conditional write primitive that can atomically guard the raw precondition without a race window. Therefore read-before-write does not eliminate all race windows; mechanical pre-read validation + single external attempt + mandatory readback verification + OUTCOME_UNKNOWN/CONFLICT handoff is required (see read-write-verify protocol).
